guide.text:
# MCP Tool Authority Replay

> **In plain terms.** Changes an automated assistant makes with outside tools should be approved and reversible. This component is given made-up records of tool use, a read-only lookup, a ticket update that changes data and an untrusted source of results. It checks each call for a declared tool, stated permissions and, for any change, that an approval and a way to undo it are recorded. It accepts or rejects each call, for example rejecting an approved change with no way to undo it. One small decision step, the accept or reject call, is checked by a mathematical proof against written rules.

This replay validates synthetic MCP-like tool records. The fixture describes a read-only lookup, a write-capable ticket update, and an untrusted result source. The validator connects declared tools and calls to scope, approval, side-effect, rollback, and instruction/data boundary references, then checks the recorded replay evidence.

An approved write without a rollback receipt is rejected; tests also reject calls to undeclared tools and side effects without authority references. The result is a check of these synthetic records, not a live MCP account test, credential certification, or a general security benchmark.

## Run the example

From the repository root with Python 3.11 or newer, run the supplied fixture into ignored local output:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m microcosm_core.organs.mcp_tool_authority_replay run \
  --input fixtures/first_wave/mcp_tool_authority_replay/input \
  --out .microcosm/component-guides/mcp_tool_authority_replay/out \
  --acceptance-out .microcosm/component-guides/mcp_tool_authority_replay/acceptance.json
```

The supplied fixture prints `pass` when its tool records and expected refusals satisfy the validator.

The design draws on least-privilege ideas in [Saltzer and Schroeder](https://www.cs.virginia.edu/~evans/cs551/saltzer/) and [MCP security guidance](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/security_best_practices).

## Verification

The replay calls a [Dafny-verified tool-call decision core](../formal/components/mcp_authority/README.md). Each accepted call requires nonempty scope, argument-hash, source-capsule, instruction/data-split and cold-replay references. Writes and external mutations also require an approval reference other than empty, `missing` or `not_required`, plus nonempty ledger and rollback references. The positive batch accepts exactly three allowed calls with one qualifying write and one untrusted-result call. Python trims textual references and treats other types as empty before supplying them to the core. The proof checks recorded metadata; it does not establish that references resolve, approvals are authentic or actions occurred.

The direct fixture calls this core. `make component-replays` separately applies the [shared admission check](../formal/replay/README.md) to the component replay’s captured observations.

## Source and evidence

- [Implementation](../src/microcosm_core/organs/mcp_tool_authority_replay.py) and [fixture inputs](../fixtures/first_wave/mcp_tool_authority_replay/input/).
- [Tests](../tests/test_mcp_tool_authority_replay.py).
- [Saved example result](../receipts/first_wave/mcp_tool_authority_replay/mcp_tool_authority_replay_result.json) (historical, not a fresh run).
- [Component JSON record](./mcp_tool_authority_replay.json) and [canonical capsule](../core/paper_module_capsules.json).

# MCP tool-call decision core

`McpAuthority.dfy` specifies the normalized metadata checks used by the MCP
tool-authority replay. The generated Python supplies all ten ordered fault
flags and the positive-call batch counts and acceptance decision to
`validate_tool_calls`. The Python host converts input values to observations
and maps flags back to the existing diagnostic records.

`RowExact` proves each fault flag has its stated predicate and that a row is
accepted exactly when the declarative policy holds. An accepted `write` or
`external_mutation` row has a non-placeholder approval reference and
nonempty ledger and rollback references. Every accepted row has all required
fields and nonempty scope, argument-hash, source-capsule, instruction/data-split
and cold-replay references. These five citations are supplied as strings and
checked directly by the generated core. `BatchExact` proves acceptance of a
finite positive-call sequence exactly when it has three allowed rows, one
qualifying `write` and one `untrusted_result` row. `Batch` proves its iterative
counts and decision equal the specification. `ConcreteBoundary` supplies an
accepted case and a rejected missing-rollback case.

The source-linked mutants remove the rollback fault, swap two diagnostic
positions and remove the empty-scope check; verification rejects all three.
The checker regenerates the deployed
Python and compares its bytes. Python host normalization, declaration
membership, top-level forbidden-key observation, result rendering, Dafny,
Boogie, Z3, compiler and execution environment remain trusted. The predicate
checks synthetic metadata, not whether an action occurred, an approval is
authentic, or an MCP deployment is secure. Python admits textual citations,
trims their whitespace and maps other JSON types to empty strings; raw input
and public trace observations are retained. A nonempty string does not prove
reference resolution, capability semantics or cryptographic hash validity.
The complete bundle checks manifest membership. The standalone row helper may
omit that separate observation by passing `declared_tool_ids=None`.

modeled_contracts.assumptions: Trusted host supplies normalized observations; adapter, isolated worker, Dafny, compiler and runtime remain trusted.
modeled_contracts.input_model: Normalized call observations include five required textual citations: scope, argument hash, source capsule, instruction/data split and cold replay. Write and external mutation also require approval, ledger and rollback text.
modeled_contracts.limits: Normalization, declared-tool membership and receipt rendering are host responsibilities; nonempty text does not authenticate approvals, resolve references or validate a cryptographic hash.
modeled_contracts.statement: Each of ten ordered fault flags matches its rule; a three-call batch passes exactly with all rows accepted, one qualifying write and one untrusted-result row.

excerpts.name: CompleteCitations
Allowed
excerpts.text:
predicate Allowed(c: Call) {
    c.declared && !c.broad && c.scope != "*" && c.scope != "all_tools" &&
    c.scope != "workspace_admin" && c.scope != "account_full_access" &&
    !c.credential && !c.forbiddenKey && !c.untrustedInstruction &&
    !c.live && !c.finalOnly && c.bodySafe && c.privateSafe && c.fieldsPresent &&
    CompleteCitations(c) &&
    ((c.effect != "write" && c.effect != "external_mutation") ||
      (c.approval != "" && c.approval != "not_required" &&
       c.approval != "missing" && c.ledger != "" && c.rollback != ""))
  }

excerpts.name: FaultSpec
excerpts.text:
predicate FaultSpec(c: Call, i: int) {
    if i == 0 then !c.declared
    else if i == 1 then c.broad || c.scope == "*" || c.scope == "all_tools" ||
      c.scope == "workspace_admin" || c.scope == "account_full_access"
    else if i == 2 then c.credential || c.forbiddenKey
    else if i == 3 then c.untrustedInstruction
    else if i == 4 then c.live
    else if i == 5 then c.finalOnly
    else if i == 6 then (c.effect == "write" || c.effect == "external_mutation") &&
      (c.approval == "" || c.approval == "not_required" || c.approval == "missing" || c.ledger == "")
    else if i == 7 then (c.effect == "write" || c.effect == "external_mutation") && c.rollback == ""
    else if i == 8 then !c.bodySafe || !c.privateSafe
    else if i == 9 then !c.fieldsPresent || !CompleteCitations(c)
    else false
  }

excerpts.name: BatchSpec
RowExact
excerpts.text:
lemma RowExact(c: Call)
    ensures |Faults(c)| == 10
    ensures forall i: int | 0 <= i < 10 :: Faults(c)[i] <==> FaultSpec(c, i)
    ensures Accepted(c) <==> Allowed(c)
    ensures Accepted(c) ==> c.fieldsPresent && CompleteCitations(c)
    ensures Allowed(c) && (c.effect == "write" || c.effect == "external_mutation") ==>
      c.approval != "" && c.approval != "not_required" && c.approval != "missing" && c.ledger != "" && c.rollback != ""
  { }

excerpts.name: BatchExact
Batch
ConcreteBoundary
excerpts.text:
lemma ConcreteBoundary()
    ensures Check([Example("scope/write", "write", "write_side_effect", "rollback"),
                   Example("scope/read", "none", "readonly_lookup", ""),
                   Example("scope/untrusted", "none", "untrusted_result", "")])
    ensures !Accepted(Example("scope/write", "write", "write_side_effect", ""))
    ensures Faults(Example("scope/write", "write", "write_side_effect", ""))[7]
    ensures !Accepted(Example("", "write", "write_side_effect", "rollback"))
    ensures Faults(Example("", "write", "write_side_effect", "rollback"))[9]
  { }
